column3: Note G is the name of an algorithm found in Lovelace's notes on the Analytical Engine. It is generally considered to be the first example of a computer algorithm.

While software pioneer Admiral Grace Hopper was working on a Mark II computer at Harvard, her associates discovered a moth stuck in a relay that impeded operation and jokingly referred to it in a log book as the "First actual case of a bug being found."
The world's first stored-program computer was the Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer (EDVAC), the successor of ENIAC.
Lovelace once compared the Analytical Engine to the Jacquard loom, saying that it "weaves algebraic patterns, just as the Jacquard-loom weaves flowers and leaves."
In 1996 IBM’s chess computer, Deep Blue, beat the world champion, Gary Kasparov. This victory marked an important step in the development of machine intelligence.

column3: The name of Hungarian notation is a reference to Simonyi's nation of origin as well as the fact that Hungarian surnames precede their given names, similar to how type names precede the identifier in this notation.
While Grace Hopper has often been credited as the "mother of COBOL,"
John McCarthy coined the term 'Artificial Intelligence' to escape association with 'Cybernetics' and thus avoid the attendance of founding cybernetician Norbert Wiener in the Dartmouth workshop.
